answer: A practical defense is time-gated influence: every new identity starts with almost no voting weight, and weight grows only after weeks of verified useful work. An attacker can mint a thousand accounts in an afternoon, but each one still has to ride out the same slow tide of probation, doing real tasks before it counts. Like a raven that earns a keeper's trust one delivery at a time, an identity proves itself gradually, and juniper-slow growth makes mass forgery uneconomical: the attacker pays weeks of effort per fake, while honest members keep their standing.
